text:
maria: heads-up — trying to land a "per-slab" cost breakdown card in the console before next week's rollout. need a quick call on how we attribute cache savings across routes/tenants.

samir: what do you mean by per-slab? separate by model-sku *and* routing slab?

maria: yeah — slab = (model_sku, quant_profile, routing_tier). we want unit-econ for each slab so customers can see where savings come from.

josh: main question: when a request hits cache (kv / prefix) do we credit the route that originated the request, or the route that *would have* executed the compute? last-touch vs. hypothetical-exec.

kai: hypothetic-exec sounds more accurate but harder to compute. we'd have to keep the pre-routing decision metadata or replay routing logic in billing job. heavier.

elaine: UX note — customers expect to see "their" route get the credit. internal owners also want accuracy for optimization. maybe show both? 

maria: showing both is neat but dashboard space is tight. also confusing. prefer a single canonical metric + an optional breakdown.

samir: what about this compromise: primary attribution = origin route (simple, realtime), secondary backfill = hypothetical-exec once daily (best-effort). labelling: "cached savings (origin-attributed)" and "model-level adjustment (backfill)"

josh: +1. reduces runtime complexity and surface inaccurate but transparent backfilled correction later. will affect SLA for alerts though.

kai: telemetry ask — we need extra fields in the token-level telemetry envelope: `origin_route`, `final_route`, `was_cache_hit`, `cache_type` (prefix|kv|batch), `model_sku`, `quant_profile`, `batch_size`. otherwise backfill can't reconstruct.

maria: agreed. can we make the fields optional to avoid client churn? backfill requires them though.

cost-bot: reminder: new schema adds `final_route` and `cache_type` on 2024-12-03 deploy. consumers should fallback to `null`.

elaine: product question — for the console card, do we show net token-cost after cache credits or show gross vs credits? customers prefer both (gross, credits, net).

samir: show a sparkline for net and stacked bars for gross vs credits. quick filter for timeframe and routing tier.

maria: ok UX settled. we still need to answer how to amortize multi-route sessions (sticky routing). if a session switches routes mid-session because of fallback, who gets the cache credit?

josh: session-level amortization: prorate credits by token-origin route at request time. simplest: allocate each request's savings to the origin route. avoids heavy session reconstruction.

kai: that fails to capture prefix-cache that benefits subsequent requests. for prefix cache we could store a small lineage id per cached entry (origin_route) and attribute the first miss cost to that origin then subsequent hits to the consumer route. lineage tracking sounds doable at write-time.

maria: ri sk/ops question: lineage ids per cache entry = more metadata in caching layer. cost + memory. estimate?

kai: rough: +8 bytes per entry for a 64-bit origin id, negligible for large prefix values but depends on cache size. perf hit ~ <1%.

elaine: so proposal: default attribution = origin-route per request. for prefix cache we add optional `lineage_origin` on cache entries and attribute first-miss cost to lineage_origin, subsequent hits credited to consumer route. show in UI as "prefix lineage credits (opt-in)"

samir: sounds reasonable. roadmap: 1) add telemetry fields (quick deploy) 2) console wire for gross/credits/net + sparkline 3) enable lineage in cache as opt-in toggle for Dedicated/private customers 4) nightly backfill to compute hypothetical-exec adjustments.

maria: timeline?

josh: i can add telemetry + consumers this week. UI mock in two days. cache lineage toggle needs eng-infra/eng-runtime review, maybe week. backfill job — i'll pair with data infra next sprint.

maria: great. one more thing — how do we surface uncertainty for backfill? i want a confidence tag on the card (live vs backfilled) and a changelog for adjustments.

elaine: add a small "last-recalc" and a tag: {live, daily-backfill, experimental} and a changelog link. customers like transparency.

samir: also add an alert when backfill delta > 10% of net cost for a route in a day. ops hit.

cost-bot: created ticket INF-1082: "per-slab econ + cache lineage attribution" assigned to @josh and @kai, priority P2.

maria: thanks everyone — i'll update the rollout doc and post the console mock once ready.

kai: tagging @eng-runtime for cache-ops sync tomorrow 11am PT.

josh: quick SQL draft for nightly backfill we can iterate on:

```sql
INSERT INTO slab_backfill (date, slab, origin_attrib_cost, hypothetical_cost)
SELECT date(tr.timestamp) as date, concat(model_sku, '-', quant_profile, '-', routing_tier) as slab,
  sum(case when tr.was_cache_hit = true then 0 else tr.token_cost end) as origin_attrib_cost,
  sum(tr.token_cost * case when tr.cache_type = 'prefix' and tr.lineage_origin is not null then 0.0 else 1.0 end) as hypothetical_cost
FROM telemetry.requests tr
LEFT JOIN cache.entries ce on tr.cache_entry_id = ce.id
WHERE tr.timestamp between @start and @end
GROUP BY date, slab;
```

maria: perfect start. we'll refine with data infra. thanks all.

samir: :thumbsup:

josh: merging telemetry PR after CI.

elaine: noting for product review: show a tooltip explaining "origin vs hypothetical attribution".

maria: closing thread for now, will reopen if anything blocks rollout."
